info.name: PrepDeck API
info.description:
Requests and tests for the PrepDeck questions API.

**Setup**
1. Run `npm run dev` in the PrepDeck repo.
2. Import this collection and `PrepDeck.local.postman_environment.json`, then select the **PrepDeck (local)** environment. Without it, the collection falls back to its own `baseUrl` of `http://localhost:3000`.
3. Run folder 1, then folder 2. Folder 3 needs `.env.local` changes; see its description.

**Auth.** There are no auth headers. The server reads identity from `DEV_USER_ID` and `DEV_USER_ROLE` in `.env.local` (default: `founder` / `admin`).

**Errors** always come back as `{ "error": { "code", "message", "details"? } }`: `VALIDATION` 400, `UNAUTHENTICATED` 401, `FORBIDDEN` 403, `NOT_FOUND` 404, `CONFLICT` 409. A collection-level test checks this on every 4xx/5xx response.

**Test data.** Folder 1 writes real questions tagged `postman`. Remove them in Atlas with `{ "source": "postman" }`.

item.name: 1. Question lifecycle
item.description:
Run top to bottom. Later requests use ids saved by earlier ones.

This writes **real questions** to the database set in `.env.local`: three per run, under topic `sandbox/postman`, tagged and sourced `postman`. There is no delete endpoint yet. Remove them in Atlas Data Explorer with the filter `{ "source": "postman" }`.

{
  "stem": "What is the difference between Terraform and Ansible, and when would you use each? [postman {{runId}}]",
  "type": "short-answer",
  "difficulty": "medium",
  "topicPath": "Sandbox/Postman",
  "tags": [
    "Terraform",
    "ansible",
    "terraform",
    "postman"

  "answer": {
    "modelAnswer": "Terraform provisions infrastructure (what exists); Ansible configures it (what runs on it). Terraform is declarative and tracks state; Ansible is procedural automation.",

      "provisioning vs configuration management",
      "Terraform state tracks desired vs actual",
      "both should be idempotent"

    "explanation": "Typical flow: Terraform creates the EC2 instance, then Ansible installs Docker on it.",
    "references": [
      "https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/intro"

  "source": "postman"
}

item.name: 3. Auth scenarios (edit .env.local first)
item.description:
Postman cannot switch users here: the server reads identity from `DEV_USER_ID` and `DEV_USER_ROLE` in `.env.local`, not from request headers.

For each subfolder, edit `.env.local` as its description says, restart `npm run dev`, then run it. Set them back to `DEV_USER_ID=founder` and `DEV_USER_ROLE=admin` when you are done.

Run folder 1 first so `{{draftQuestionId}}` is set. If you forget to change `.env.local`, these requests fail without changing any data.

item.description: In `.env.local`, comment out `DEV_USER_ID`, then restart `npm run dev`.
